items.title: Pete Levin interviewed by Monk Rowe, Danbury, Connecticut, November 20, 2001
items.q: My first stint with Gil Evans I was playing French horn... I was in the band for fifteen years.

ctx.x: But I was advised a lot in school, and it made sense to me at the time so I got an education degree and finished. And I kind of sensed there was a gap in my performance experience. So I just said well let me — before I teach, let me go on to Juilliard, I’ll just get another degree or whatever, or let me just play some more. And that put me into the New York scene and I started playing with better ensembles and on the side I subbed for © Fillius Jazz Archive -3-
Gil Evans and discovered this whole new world, and finally realized I don’t want to teach. So I got there eventually. But I didn’t know from the beginning is the short answer. Sorry I took so long.
